text:
Tom P: Quick sync — I'm proposing a rollout plan for the experimental degrade + traffic-sculpting feature. Goal: surface partial fallbacks when backend cost/latency spikes, and shape traffic by region/cohort. High-level plan below.

Maria G: +1. Can we make the canary gradual and safety-gated? Suggested: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% over multiple windows with automatic rollback triggers.

Alex H: Strong yes to safety gates. Proposed metrics to watch: 95th latency, p95 error delta, model quality drift (BLEU/embedding drift proxies), and customer-facing error rate. Revert if p95 increases > 30% or error delta > 0.5pp.

Jon R: For enterprise/dedicated customers we need an explicit opt-in flag and a manual approval step in the console. They can't be silently switched. Also: document fallback SLAs.

Lina C: For A/B experiments we should include a holdback arm that only gets traffic-sculpting heuristics but not behavioral degrade. That lets us measure regressions separately.

Tom P: Agree. Draft rollout sequence: 1) Internal dev + devex 2) Canary (1% global) 3) Regional expansion (EU/NA/APAC slices) 4) A/B ramp with holdback cohort 5) Enterprise opt-ins -> GA. Time windows and thresholds below.

ProductOps: Proposed thresholds and window:
- Canary window = 2h per step
- Ramp steps: 1% (2h) -> 5% (4h) -> 20% (6h) -> steady 48h monitoring
- Automatic rollback if: p95 latency increase >= 30% vs baseline OR customer error-rate delta >= 0.5pp OR automated quality regression alert fires

Tom P: Flagging the actual feature-flag names and control surfaces. Example flag payload posted for infra team: 
```
{
  "flag": "features.experimental_degrade_v1",
  "cohorts": ["global-1pct","global-5pct","region-eu-5pct"],
  "fallback_policy": "route-to-stable-model",
  "max_retries": 1
}
```

Maria G: Can we add a TTL for canary cohorts so stale cohorts are garbage-collected? And make the flag revocable via the console toggle (manual kill-switch).

Alex H: Add a routing priority list in fallback_policy: [stable-model, quantized-variant, cached-response]. Also record reason codes on fallback for telemetry.

Jon R: For dedicated customers, different JSON: 
```
{
  "flag": "features.experimental_degrade_v1",
  "scope": "tenant:explicit",
  "requires_approval": true
}
```

Lina C: Observability: create a per-cohort dashboard with these panels: request volume, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, fallback rate, top fallback reasons, quality eval pass rate. Also include per-tenant heatmap.

ProductOps: Launch gating checklist draft (must pass before each ramp):
- Metrics: No rollback triggers in previous window
- Quality: No regression > threshold on eval prompt set
- Capacity: Serving pool headroom >= 20%
- Docs: Release notes + admin toggle documented
- Enterprise comms: Notify tenants with dedicated infra 48h prior

Tom P: Scope negotiation: we will ship MVP with basic route->stable fallback and traffic slices by region. Things deferred to post-GA: automated model fallback ordering, ML-driven sculpting heuristics (will be feature-bumped). Keep that on backlog.

Maria G: Customer-driven asks: Two customers asked for per-tenant custom thresholds. Could we expose per-tenant overrides (alpha) behind a flag? That will add complexity but high-value for a few early customers.

Jon R: We can do per-tenant overrides but enforce guardrails: overrides can't increase allowed error delta beyond global safety cap. Also require a signed SLA amendment for any override that relaxes safety.

Alex H: Operational playbook snippet for rollbacks: 
1) ProductOps toggle -> pause cohort
2) Infra autoscale buffer -> spin up extra nodes (if needed)
3) If repeat regressions, route all traffic to stable-model and open incident

ProductOps: Action items:
- @Maria G: create canary dashboards and quality eval set (ETA: tomorrow noon)
- @Alex H: add fallback reason codes and telemetry (ETA: 48h)
- @Jon R: add tenant opt-in flow + approval UX mock (ETA: EOD Friday)
- @Lina C: prepare A/B analysis template and holdback cohort config (ETA: Monday)

SRE-Bot: deploy-bot: Canary job queued for features.experimental_degrade_v1 -> cohort global-1pct.

Tom P: Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after first canary window to evaluate metrics. :thumbsup:
